analogs.covers: Life and temperament: a cunning, skittish opportunist living in a family group with a dominant breeder
Mischief: sneaky, masked, same-sex gangs, always on the lookout for an easy meal

headline: A cunning, skittish fox family that turns dangerous in a group, with a raccoon's sneakiness.

setting.label: Woods, hills and dry canyons
setting.note: Sedentary; the dominant male leads the leash whenever it relocates. Optional chromatophores let it blend into its surroundings.

playsLike: You are a medium carnivore in a 'leash': a dominant male with his breeding group and their grown offspring, up to 8. Alone you prefer to scavenge and hunt up to Medium tier; 2–4 of you hunt Large; a full party of 5 can take solitary Apex herbivores. Hunts are bait-and-dart: one calls and postures as bait while the others dart in for bleeding bites. You are skittish and always flee Apex carnivores, and subordinates sneak courtship behind the boss's back.

why.text: A group of foxes is called a 'leash', and fox families keep grown offspring as helpers around the breeding animals (official inspiration: foxes).
Solitary animals prefer to scavenge, even from claimed corpses, and always put their own life first.
Always flees Apex carnivores and flees anything its group is too small to hunt.
Same-sex 'mask' groups and sneaky courtship by subordinates carry the raccoon's masked, mischievous streak (official inspiration).
One member reveals itself and calls loudly as bait while hidden packmates dart in to land bleeding bites.

notLike: Foxes don't hunt in groups; a full Dilophosaurus party can bleed down a solitary Apex herbivore.
twist: Optional chameleon-style colour shifting to blend in and regulate temperature (official inspiration).
